market_overview: Indian markets closed lower with Nifty at 24,615 (-0.64%) and Sensex at 78,429 (-0.27%), ending a four-day rally amid profit-booking in banking, IT and FMCG. Metals showed relative strength while caution prevailed ahead of the RBI MPC outcome expected in the next session. Data on exact open-high-low for Nifty is based on consensus wrap levels as live intraday details were limited.

summary.headline: 4th straight gain · Nifty hits 5-month high · Crude drop + FII buying

market_overview: Indian equities extended gains for a fourth consecutive session. Nifty closed at 24,774 (+1.60%) and Sensex at 78,639 (+0.70%), driven by a sharp fall in crude oil prices and renewed FII buying. IT was the clear sector leader. This was also the first trading day under SEBI’s new Closing Auction Session (CAS) mechanism for F&O stocks.

drivers.text: Brent tumbled ~4.6–5% on easing West Asia geopolitical tensions, reducing inflation and import bill concerns.
FIIs bought ₹922 Cr, DIIs ₹1,517 Cr — strong institutional support after recent selling.
Nifty IT surged 2.5–3.3%. TCS, Infosys and other heavyweights led the charge.

global_cues: Positive risk sentiment after crude correction and hopes of diplomatic progress on Iran. US markets had closed higher on Friday.
outlook: Strong breakout session. New Closing Auction Session (CAS) mechanism implemented.
Broad-based buying except Media. Midcap and Smallcap also hit fresh highs.
Momentum can continue if crude stays soft and FIIs remain buyers.
